description:
FOUND s438 (Opus 5) in the #473 cpan-t census population
(cpan-tests/modules/Text-CSV-2.04/t/78_fragment.t:101).

REPRO (two lines, no module):

  local $_ = "a";  my $x = $_.2;   # perl: x=[a2]   PCL: statement dropped
  my $y  = "b";    my $z = $y.5;   # perl: z=[b5]   PCL: statement dropped
                                   # "Bug. Fell through. Missing case: ["

PPI 1.291's token stream for `my $x = $_.2;`:

  PPI::Token::Word          my
  PPI::Token::Symbol        $x
  PPI::Token::Operator      =
  PPI::Token::Magic         $_
  PPI::Token::Number::Float .2        <-- perl reads `.` as concat, `2` as 2
  PPI::Token::Structure     ;

There is no `.` OPERATOR in the stream, so the term walker sees SYMBOL NUMBER
juxtaposed and falls through.  perl's own toke.c only starts a number at `.`
when a term is expected; after a complete term, `.` is the concatenation
operator.  A space (`$_ . 2`) or a non-digit (`$_."2"`) makes both lex it
correctly -- the bug needs the digit to be adjacent.

LAYER: PPI upstream (rule 13).  The workaround is the `_repair_*` family in
Pl/Parser.pm (the same shape as #351/#354/#361: split the Number::Float back
into an Operator `.` plus a Number when the previous significant token ENDS A
TERM).  The one to be careful about is `.5` where a term is NOT expected --
i.e. exactly the discriminator `_ends_term` already answers for #457's `)-name`.

WHEN THE WORKAROUND LANDS: docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md gains its section and
docs/ppi-bug-report.t gains a failing row (rule 13, same commit), and the
census row for 78_fragment.t leaves by EDIT.

DONE s456ag (Opus agent AG, round 13).  Fixed as the task sketched, in the
`_repair_*` family: `Pl::Parser2::_repair_dot_number` splits a `PPI::Token::Number`
whose content starts `.<digit>` back into an Operator `.` plus the number when
the previous significant token `_ends_term`, then reparses -- the fourth member
of the family after Â§12 `)*name`, Â§15 `)-1` and Â§25 `)-name`, and the same
predicate.

ONE POSITION NEEDED AN EXCEPTION THE SHAPE ORACLE CANNOT SEE, and it is the
case the first version BROKE (found by probing what the change could break, not
what it fixes): a `print`/`printf`/`say` FILEHANDLE is shaped like a completed
term and is not one -- perl is still waiting for the argument list, so
`print $fh .5` writes the NUMBER 0.5 and `print $x .5` treats $x as the handle
(probed).  `Pl::Parser2::_is_print_filehandle_slot` is that exception: a `$`
Symbol whose own previous significant token is print/printf/say.  It has ONE
consumer deliberately -- the sibling repairs can reach the same position
(`print $fh -3` is task #405, already filed) but narrowing their shared oracle
`_ends_term` is a wider change, and no site exists in any of the four
populations.  A BAREWORD handle (`print STDOUT .5`) and the block form
(`print {$fh} .5`) need no guard: `_ends_term` already answers 0 for both.

PROBES vs perl 5.40.3, all identical: 8 positives ($_.2, $y.5, $a[1].3,
$h{k}.4, f().6, $#a.7, "r".8, $r->[0].1), 11 negatives (= .5, (1,.5),
(a => .5), return .5, -.5, [.5], f(.5), 1.5, 1..5, 2 . .5, "x" x 2 .9) and
the 5 print-filehandle rows.

MEASURED: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111; emission A/B vs 83b335f over the
cpan + perl-t + lib + board populations -- Text-CSV-2.04/t/78_fragment.t the
only file this change moves; gate-SET scan over both populations shows no
verdict change for it (it is not in the gate SET).  Census row for
78_fragment.t left BY EDIT; the cpan-`t` population is now at ZERO drops.

RULE 13 PAID IN THE SAME COMMIT: docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§28 (repro, token
dump, the spaced control, PCL impact) + 4 rows in docs/ppi-bug-report.t (bug 28:
two failing rows, two controls -- the spaced spelling and the `= .5` negative).
Guard rows: Pl/t/minus-word-01.t 10 -> 20 (5 positives, 5 negatives incl. the
two print-filehandle ones); the positives fail on a base tree.
subject: PPI lexes `$var.2` as SYMBOL + Number::Float(.2) -- no concatenation operator at all, so every `$x.<digit>` statement DROPS (found in the new cpan-t census population)
